subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Land Rover Defender
description: A quick, practical guide to The Land Rover Defender.

hook.text: The original Land Rover was sketched in sand on a beach in Wales. It became a legend in mud.

buildup.text: Inspired by the Willys Jeep, Maurice Wilks designed it as a farm tool—rugged, simple, unstoppable.

discovery.text: Its aluminum body (steel was rationed post-war) accidentally made it rust-resistant for decades.

twist.text: It became the vehicle of choice for armies, aid workers, and explorers on every continent.

climax.text: When production ended in 2016, workers signed the last one. Over two million had been built.

punchline.text: A farm tool became the most traveled car in history.

quiz.question: Why did the original Land Rover use an aluminum body?
options: Steel was rationed after the war

details.summary: The Land Rover Defender, born in 1948 as a rugged utility vehicle for farms and military forces, became the ultimate symbol of go-anywhere capability and served in over 150 countries worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: The Defender proved that simple, durable engineering could create a vehicle trusted in the world's toughest environments, from Antarctic expeditions to African safaris and military operations.
takeaways: The original was inspired by the American Willys Jeep
Its aluminum body was chosen due to postwar steel shortages
The classic model was produced for 67 years until 2016

faq.question: Why was the Defender discontinued and then brought back?
faq.answer: The original could not meet modern safety and emissions regulations without compromises to its character. The new 2020 Defender is a completely different vehicle underneath, combining capability with modern standards.

faq.question: Is the new Defender as capable off-road as the old one?
faq.answer: In many ways yes, and in some ways more so thanks to modern electronics. However, purists miss the original's simplicity and field-repairability that made it ideal in remote locations without workshops.
